LESSON: FRACTIONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.6: Fractions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Fractions. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compare fractions in different situations
2. order fractions with denominators not exceeding 12 in different situations
3. add two fractions with the same denominator in different situations
4. subtract two fractions with the same denominator in different situations
5. add two fractions with one renaming in different situations, g) subtract two fractions with one renaming in different situations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT FRACTIONS MEAN
A fraction names equal parts of a whole. In 1/2, the whole is split into 2 equal parts and you take 1.

WORKED EXAMPLES
A: Shade 1/4 of a rectangle divided into 4 equal parts.
B: 1/2 of 12 mangoes = 6 mangoes.
C: 1/4 of 20 = 5.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: 1/2 of 12 = 6

Example 2: 1/4 of 20 = 5

Example 3: 3/4 means 3 equal parts out of 4

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Fractions.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Fractions in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. compare fractions in different situations
2. order fractions with denominators not exceeding 12 in different situations
3. add two fractions with the same denominator in different situations
4. subtract two fractions with the same denominator in different situations

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
